To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a Redundancy-reduced MobileNet (RR-mobileNet), which is a more compact and efficient version of MobileNet, and we implement it in a FPGA platform to demonstrate that the proposed design can significantly reduce memory traffic and improve performance.
we propose a Redundancy Reduced MobileNet which is 25× smaller and 9%/5% more accurate compared to AlexNet.
we propose an efficient hardware design for a redundancy-reduced MobileNet which is suitable for low-power applications such as mobile devices and embedded systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient system architectures for image classification on reconfigurable logic.
the efficient implementation of CNNs in power-efficient embedded applications.

the following contributions: (1) we propose a new system architecture for MobileNet, which can be used as a baseline for further research on low-power CNN accelerators; (2) we propose a method for reducing the model size and the computational complexity of MobileNet; (3) we implement the proposed system design in a Xilinx Zynq-7000 FPGA and evaluate its performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed system design can achieve high classification accuracy with a low power consumption.
our RR-MobileNet is a promising solution for image classification applications with limited on-chip resources and low system latency.
the RR-MobileNet is 25x smaller, 3.5x faster and 3x power-efficient than AlexNet on FPGA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed an efficient system design to accelerate modern CNNs on FPGAs with low power consumption, and the proposed design has the potential to be applied to other CNN models.
we propose a system design with low memory traffic and low computational complexity for a redundancy-reduced MobileNet, which can be used for image classification on resource-constrained platforms.

we propose an efficient system architecture for a redundancy-reduced MobileNet, which is suitable for low-power applications such as smart phones, wearable devices, and Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed system design for RR-MobileNet can be easily extended to other CNN models, and can be implemented in FPGA platforms with low power and high performance.
the redundancy in modern CNN models can be reduced significantly without sacrificing accuracy, and the resulting system design can achieve a much higher system performance.
, by removing model redundancy, we can significantly accelerate modern CNNs for real-time image classification applications.
